title: "Width and gap"
description: "A figure sets an absolute width and a wider gap."
format:
  html: default
  pdf: default
  typst:

  docx: default
---

The figure on this page sets an absolute width and a gap of `2em`, twice
the default:

```markdown
![Mean ratings.](ratings.png){#fig-ratings .wrap-left width="2.5in" wrap-gap="2em"}
```

## Result

![Mean ratings.](../images/ratings.png){#fig-ratings .wrap-left width="2.5in" wrap-gap="2em"}

@fig-ratings is 2.5 inches wide in each of the four formats. In HTML, a
window at the breakpoint or narrower gives it the full width of the text
column instead. An absolute length does
not change with the width of the text, so in a narrow text column the
figure takes a larger share of the line.

The gap between the figure and this text is `2em`, twice the default of
`1em`. Each format converts both values to its own units.

A percent width, such as the default 40%, is a share of the text width
instead. Use a percent when the same document renders to pages of
different widths.
